blocks.text: Functional disorders affect the normal working of the nervous system without any apparent structural or organic cause.

A headache is pain or discomfort in the head or neck. Primary headaches are due to the headache itself, not another cause, for example migraine and tension headache. Secondary headaches are due to an underlying structural problem in the head or neck, such as bleeding in the brain, a tumour or meningitis. Treatment includes pain-killing (analgesic) medicines, reducing stress, regular exercise and better sleep habits.

blocks.title: Migraine
blocks.text: Migraine is a headache with intense, throbbing pain on one side or in one region of the head, caused by changes in the brain and its blood vessels that lead to inflammation and pain.

blocks.prompt: Is a headache caused by meningitis primary or secondary?
blocks.explanation: Secondary: it is due to an underlying problem, the inflamed meninges.

items: Functional disorders: no structural cause. Headache: primary (migraine, tension) or secondary (bleeding, tumour, meningitis); analgesics, less stress, exercise, sleep.
